summary: Redis cache deployment is scaled to 0 replicas, causing all product and catalog cache lookups in inventory to time out and fall back directly to PostgreSQL. This database load spike exhausted inventory's HikariCP connection pool and saturated Postgres CPU, leading to cascading request timeouts in inventory, orders, and the gateway.

leads: Check gateway logs for upstream request failed or upstream request timed out messages to see which downstream service is failing. (runbook:triage-high-error-rate)
Check http_server_requests_seconds_count with outcome SERVER_ERROR to see which service is returning 5xx responses. (runbook:triage-high-error-rate)
Check gateway UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS and upstream request latency to see if requests are timing out. (runbook:gateway-upstream)

related.text:
- An alert like "orders: 12% of requests are failing".
- `http_server_requests_seconds_count{outcome="SERVER_ERROR"}` rising for one or
  more services.
- Callers log failed calls. The gateway logs "upstream request failed" (502) or
  "upstream request timed out" (504).
related.title: HighErrorRate: a service is returning 5xx

related.text:
The gateway proxies `/api` requests to orders and inventory, with one upstream
timeout for all routes (`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS`, normally 4000 ms). It answers 502
"upstream request failed" when it can't reach an upstream, and 504 "upstream
request timed out" when the upstream doesn't answer in time. It logs every
failure with the timeout and the error.
related.title: Gateway 502 and 504 responses

related.text:
- An alert like "orders: p95 latency is 2.3s".
- Callers' outgoing call latency (`http_client_requests_seconds`) rises together
  with the callee's server latency.
- Once latency passes a caller's timeout it turns into errors: the gateway
  returns 504 "upstream request timed out", and HikariCP logs "Connection is not
  available, request timed out after 2000ms".
related.title: HighLatency: p95 above one second

triage.summary: Gateway, inventory, and orders services are experiencing high error rates affecting users.

hypotheses.summary: The Redis cache deployment is scaled down to 0 replicas, causing cache operations in inventory to time out and fall back to PostgreSQL. The resulting surge in database queries exhausted inventory's connection pool and saturated Postgres CPU, causing high latency and cascading request timeouts across inventory, orders, and gateway.

evidence.shows: Redis deployment is scaled down to 0 desired replicas, making Redis completely unavailable.

evidence.quote: Cannot reconnect to [redis/<unresolved>:6379]: Connection refused (connect failed): redis.sandbox.svc.cluster.local/10.96.138.16:6379
evidence.shows: Inventory service fails to connect to Redis due to connection refusal.

evidence.quote: Redis cache GET failed for catalog::top100, falling back to database: RedisCommandTimeoutException: Command timed out after 250 millisecond(s)
evidence.shows: Inventory Redis cache reads time out and fall back to PostgreSQL database queries.
PostgreSQL connection pool on inventory is exhausted due to cache misses falling back to database, saturating Postgres CPU and causing inventory timeouts.

evidence.quote: POST /orders failed: inventory POST /inventory/reserve timed out: no response within 1000 ms
evidence.shows: Orders service fails as downstream calls to inventory time out.
Gateway requests fail with 504 gateway timeouts due to slow upstream responses from inventory and orders.

hypotheses.suggested_fix: Scale the Redis deployment replicas up to 1 (e.g., kubectl scale deployment/redis --replicas=1 -n sandbox) to restore the cache and alleviate database load.

review.reason: The evidence directly shows that the Redis deployment was scaled down to 0 desired replicas, causing Redis connection refusals and cache timeouts in inventory. This forced inventory to fall back to PostgreSQL queries, saturating its DB connection pool and causing cascading downstream timeouts in orders and gateway.
